## What changed and why

Task #446 is done and merged at 298727a. It fixed the blocking finding 1 of review #443.
`check()` in `benchmark/scripts/split_allocate.py` now returns the count of completed controls. `main()` requires exactly 8: 1 reason self-test and 7 mutation rejections.
The four probes of #446 (b, b2, a, c) exit 1. Evidence: [#446 report](../.github/loop/data/session-reports/446/e74db3cfee5afe017bb37aef5126832bb96463fc3946bc228731218ac76bde8c.json).
I measured these SHA256 values with `python3 -I`:

| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| split_allocate.py | 55c236ad… |
| allocation.synthetic.json | 70d94d28… (unchanged) |
| preparation.json | 99069d8d… |
| preparation-status.json | 8f64e982… |

The allocator is not pinned yet. The #446 author was mainly codex GPT.

I ordered one task: `rereview-split-completion-446` (reviewer, medium effort, 40 min, 30 turns, starts from main, no exports).
Expected gain: an independent `verdict:` on finding 1 only, with 4 new probes and the actual model family.
The next Policymaker reads the verdict and the probe table. If the verdict is accept, a hash-gated script pins both allocator files under the split milestone.

Owner request #430 (method assessment) is still pending. The loop does not wait for it. Reader implementation stays gated.
Missing coverage stays visible: no native answers (#169), no executed benchmark, and no real split cases. Product quality is not measured.
Subscription quota use is not measured. I made no change to routing.

## What next

- Saved: `.session/orders.json` (parse-checked) and `policy/working-memory.md` section 0085.
- If the verdict is revise, do fix round 2 as a Policymaker script. If a further blocking finding appears, re-scope the work. Do not order a third blind fix.
- Do not repeat the #443 specification review, the F3 enumeration or the determinism check.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
